Heated gemstones are generally less valuable than their unheated counterparts when comparing stones of otherwise equal quality, because treatments like heating reduce rarity and natural appeal [d1,d2,d4,d6,d8]. For many colored gemstones such as rubies and sapphires, heated stones can lose roughly half their value compared to unheated stones with the same color and clarity [d8]. In specific cases like tanzanite, however, heat treatment is so common and difficult to detect that it may not materially affect price, since nearly all tanzanite has been heated in some way [d5].
